title: Signal deconvolution eval protocol for config and rollout attribution
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: We currently detect quality regressions after model/config rollouts using cohort-averaged eval changes and alerting thresholds. This approach conflates signal from multiple simultaneous changes (prompt config, quantization profile, kernel selection, and model variant) and is noisy for medium-sized rollouts (~5-25% traffic). Goal: design and implement a reproducible evaluation protocol that attributes deltas in eval metrics to individual config/model changes by treating the problem as a signal deconvolution task across cohorts and controlled synthetic anchors.

Scope: prototype a: (1) synthetic-anchor cohorts that inject deterministic, small-churn reference prompts across rollout buckets; (2) LLM-critic ensemble with calibrated confidence outputs used as the primary judge for subjective categories; (3) a statistical deconvolution layer that estimates per-change effect sizes and uncertainty using hierarchical Bayesian shrinkage and permutation baselines.

Approach:
- Synthetic anchors: build a small set (50-200) of semantically diverse, deterministic prompts that are stable across models and designed to elicit signals sensitive to config changes (e.g., tokenization-sensitive examples, long-context KV hits, numeric precision). These anchors will be included in production evaluation sampling and recorded at request-level.
- LLM-critic ensemble: combine 3 different judge models (open-weight variety) with diverse prompting strategies (direct rubric scoring, pairwise preference, multi-question decomposition). Each judge emits categorical rubric scores and a calibrated confidence scalar. We'll calibrate judge confidence using isotonic regression on a held-out adjudication set to produce well-calibrated probabilities.
- Deconvolution engine: treat the observed metric vector across rollout segments as a linear combination of latent change effects plus noise. Fit a hierarchical Bayesian model with priors informed by historical rollout magnitudes and anchor stability. For faster iteration, provide an accompanying frequentist bootstrap routine for initial estimates. Output: per-change mean effect, 95% credible/confidence interval, and Delta-signal-to-noise ratio.

Acceptance criteria:
- Implementation produces per-change effect estimates for at least 3 simultaneous config deltas in synthetic canary experiments with simulated traffic (reliably recovers injected effects within 15% error).
- LLM-critic ensemble calibration achieves expected calibration error (ECE) < 6% on adjudication set.
- Observability: Console dashboard (prototype) shows per-change estimated effect with CI and a human-readable explanation of top contributing prompts/cohorts.
- Alerts: Integrate with existing regression alerts such that estimated effect > threshold and CI excludes zero triggers a high-priority alert.

Telemetry & metrics to capture:
- Anchor stability score (variance over time), judge calibration ECE, model-critic agreement rate, deconvolution posterior width, time-to-detect for injected regressions, false positive rate on held-out stable periods.

Risks & mitigations:
- Judges may correlate, reducing ensemble benefit. Mitigate by enforcing model/strategy diversity and monitoring effective ensemble size.
- Anchors might leak into production prompts. Keep anchors small and avoid sensitive data; rotate periodically and monitor for collision.
- Bayesian model runtime could be slow. Provide a fast bootstrap fallback for alerting, and run full posterior nightly.

Rollout plan: prototype in staging with synthetic traffic (2 weeks) -> run closed pilot on 1 internal product with canaries (4 weeks) -> iterate on scoring rubric and calibration (2 weeks) -> expand to auto-alerting on platform (3 weeks).
